record.context_brief: Hyperbolic manifolds: isospectral but not strongly isospectral
record.original_question: Do there exist hyperbolic manifolds that are isospectral for the Laplace-Beltrami operator on functions but are not strongly isospectral, meaning that some natural elliptic operators on associated bundles have different spectra?

evidence.quote: Question 8.10. Are there isospectral hyperbolic manifolds that are not strongly isospectral?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a closed (or finite-volume) hyperbolic manifold, i.e. a complete Riemannian manifold of constant sectional curvature $-1$. Two such manifolds $M_1$ and $M_2$ are said to be:

(a) isospectral if the Laplace–Beltrami operator acting on smooth functions has the same spectrum (counted with multiplicities) on $M_1$ and on $M_2$;

(b) strongly isospectral if, for every natural elliptic differential operator $D$ that is canonically associated to the Riemannian structure and acts on sections of a natural vector bundle (for example the Hodge Laplacian on $p$-forms for each $p$, the Dirac operator when applicable, or any operator obtained by the Sunada-type construction from a representation of the isometry group of a common Riemannian cover), the spectra of $D$ on $M_1$ and on $M_2$ coincide.

Equivalently, in the locally symmetric setting $M_i = \Gamma_i \backslash \mathbb{H}^n$, strong isospectrality requires that for every finite-dimensional representation $\tau$ of the maximal compact subgroup $K = \mathrm{SO}(n)$ of $G = \mathrm{SO}(n,1)^\circ$, the spectra of the corresponding Bochner-type Laplacian on the bundle $\Gamma_i \backslash (G \times_K V_\tau)$ agree for $i = 1, 2$.

Question: Do there exist a pair of hyperbolic manifolds $M_1, M_2$ that are isospectral in the sense of (a) but not strongly isospectral in the sense of (b)?
artifact.status_search_result: Standard constructions of isospectral hyperbolic manifolds (Sunada's method, Vignéras' arithmetic constructions, Garoufalidis–Reid examples) all produce strongly isospectral pairs, since they yield representation-equivalent subgroups of a common cover. A web search did not surface any construction or proof in the literature producing isospectral hyperbolic manifolds that fail to be strongly isospectral, nor a proof that none exist; the question appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Constructing multi-cusped hyperbolic manifolds that are isospectral and not isometric
status_evidence.snippet: Pairs of isospectral non-isometric hyperbolic 3-manifolds are constructed via Sunada-type methods, which yield strongly isospectral examples.
status_evidence.claim: Known constructions of isospectral hyperbolic manifolds proceed by Sunada-type methods and produce strongly isospectral pairs, so they do not address the question.

status_evidence.title: Constructing 1-cusped isospectral non-isometric hyperbolic 3-manifolds (Garoufalidis–Reid)
status_evidence.snippet: Pairs of 1-cusped hyperbolic 3-manifolds that are isospectral but not isometric are produced; the construction is representation-equivalent and hence strongly isospectral.
status_evidence.claim: Existing isospectral hyperbolic examples are strongly isospectral, leaving the question of whether non-strongly-isospectral isospectral hyperbolic manifolds exist open.
